result:
If I had to pick one thing, I'd probably choose something upstream of most other problems: making it dramatically easier for people to change their minds when they encounter good evidence, and harder to be manipulated by bad arguments.

I keep coming back to this because so much suffering isn't caused by a shortage of solutions. We often know roughly what would reduce poverty, disease, conflict, and environmental damage. The bottleneck is frequently that people can't agree on what's true, or won't update when they're shown they're wrong, or get captured by whoever tells the most emotionally satisfying story. A world where people were even modestly better at reasoning together would fix a lot of things I'd otherwise have to pick between.

I'll admit it's a slightly nerdy answer. Someone else might reasonably say "end extreme poverty" or "cure all disease," and those are more concrete and more obviously kind. Part of me is drawn to those too, especially the poverty one, since it's so solvable and the scale of preventable misery is hard to justify. But I suspect the concrete fixes stick better when the underlying capacity to solve problems improves.

What would you pick? I'm curious whether you'd go for a specific fix or something more foundational.
